short: A massive Central Powers breakthrough shattered the Russian lines, leading to the Great Retreat of 1915.
full:
On 2 May 1915, a combined German and Austro-Hungarian offensive opened with a devastating artillery bombardment against Russian positions between Gorlice and Tarnów in Galicia. Conceived as a localized attack to relieve pressure on the Austro-Hungarian army, the assault achieved complete tactical surprise. The poorly equipped Russian defenders were overwhelmed, and their front rapidly collapsed.

What began as a tactical breakthrough evolved into a strategic rout. The Central Powers pushed relentlessly eastward, recapturing Galicia and seizing most of Russian Poland. This "Great Retreat" cost the Imperial Russian Army over a million casualties and massive losses in materiel, severely damaging Russian morale and political stability in the years preceding the 1917 revolutions.
